private, for‐ profit education may be beneficial, but is not a solution, to the problem of poor access and quality of education.

private, for‐ profit education can provide a route to ‘education for all’ in developing countries if it can be made to work.

the potential for a low‐cost, for‐profit sector to benefit the poor in India.
the question of whether a low‐cost for‐profit private sector can provide a route towards universal primary education.
whether private education can benefit the poor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for‐profit private sector provision of education may be beneficial for the poor in developing country settings, and that it is not a priori objectionable.
private education may not be beneficial to the poorest, but it may well be beneficial to the next tier of the poor and may well have benefits to the poor as a whole.
private, for‐ profit education can have a role in developing countries, and in low‐income urban areas of India.

private, for‐ profit education may be beneficial for the poor, although it cannot be a panacea for all educational problems in the developing world.
